steps.title: Create a Partner account and a dev store
steps.detail: Create a Shopify Partner account, then a development store for testing. Do not test a public app in a live merchant store first.
steps.blockerTip: A dev store lets you install and uninstall safely. A live store install cannot be undone as easily.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, create the app, set App URL, and set Allowed redirection URLs. For CLI apps, set scopes and redirect URLs in shopify.app.toml and deploy.
steps.blockerTip: For CLI apps, the app file is the source of truth. A dashboard change alone may not apply if the file is redeployed.

steps.title: Set scopes, minimum only
steps.detail: Set access scopes for the resources you actually use, for example read_products or read_orders. Remove scopes you do not need.
steps.blockerTip: Overbroad scopes slow review and increase risk. Each field needs the scope that grants it.

steps.title: Get client ID and secret from Credentials
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, open the app, Settings, Credentials, and copy Client ID and Client secret. Store the secret server side. Shopify also calls these API key and API secret.
steps.blockerTip: Never put the secret in browser code. Shopify signs webhooks with it, so it also verifies webhook requests.

steps.title: Install in the dev store and test
steps.detail: Install the app in the dev store from the Partner Dashboard install link. The merchant approves scopes, Shopify redirects with a code, and your app exchanges it for a token. Test one API call with the token in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header.
steps.blockerTip: Do not ask the merchant to type a myshopify.com URL. Shopify supplies the shop parameter in install links.
